name: Slow Cooker Turkey Zuppa Toscana
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Cream, potato and kale soup that lands well over 500 cal naturally, and the copycat name carries real search demand. Verified 8-serving page with no macros published, so est_cal is my estimate from the cup of heavy cream. Confidence: page high, calories medium. The turkey-sausage gap is the one blocker to a clean board build. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Smoked Turkey Sausage: [BUMP x1.6] source ~1 lb sausage for 8; lean turkey sausage needs ~100 g/serving for the 25 g floor
intro_html: This is the soup that keeps people coming back to a certain endless-breadstick chain, and it is four ingredients in a trench coat: sausage, potatoes, kale, and cream. Made with smoked turkey sausage in a slow cooker, it costs a fraction of the restaurant version and you do not have to listen to anybody else's birthday song. Each bowl runs {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Chicken Broth, 2.4 cartons: ~$3.45. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 3 32oz cartons.
Pantry seasonings (cayenne pepper, italian seasoning, salt, black pepper): ~$0.18. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $36.79 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.63 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $43.07 across 14 servings, roughly $3.08 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $13.35 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $56.42. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). A single bowl at the restaurant costs several times what one of these does, and you would still have to drive there.
shop_smart: Smoked turkey sausage is over half the cost here. Watch for the ropes to go on the two for one deal, since they freeze for months in their sealed packaging.
Potatoes by the 6 pound bag are the cheapest bulk you can buy and this soup eats a lot of them. Buy the bag, keep them cool and dark, and they will still be good weeks later.
One bunch of kale is all you need. Strip the leaves from the stems, and add it at the very end so it stays green instead of turning to seaweed.
Heavy cream is the finish and it is worth every penny. Milk will break in a soup this hot and acidic, so this is not the place to save a couple dollars.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in the olive oil in a skillet. Browning takes ten minutes and it is the single biggest flavor step in this recipe, so do not skip it just because a slow cooker is involved.
Move the sausage into the slow cooker, then cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same skillet for 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, and add those too.
Cut the potatoes into half-inch thick slices and add them to the cooker with the chicken broth, the italian seasoning, cayenne, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3, until the potatoes are completely tender and starting to soften at the edges.
Stir in the chopped kale and cook 15 minutes more, just long enough for it to wilt and turn deep green.
Turn the cooker off, then stir in the heavy cream. Adding it at the end and off the boil is what keeps it from separating into curds.
Let it stand 10 minutes to thicken, then move it into your weighed pot.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is your per-container gram target. Stir the pot between scoops so the potatoes and sausage stay evenly distributed and nobody ends up with a container of cream broth. Each bowl lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Slice and brown the smoked turkey sausage in olive oil, then move it to the slow cooker.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan and add them to the cooker.
Add sliced potatoes, chicken broth, italian seasoning, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Cook on low 6 hours until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the kale for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and stir in the heavy cream.
Rest 10 minutes and portion by weight into 14 containers.
